policy_title: Ensure Schools Follow Guidance for Gender Questioning Students
stated: The Conservative Party will pass legislation to ensure schools must follow guidance for teachers on supporting gender questioning students, clarifying parents' right to know if their child wants to be treated as the opposite sex and involving them in decisions.

source.quote: In recent years, an increasing number of children have started questioning their gender, the consequences of which are still unknown. This is why we will pass legislation to ensure schools must follow our guidance for teachers on how best to support gender questioning students in schools and colleges. Parents will have a right to know if their child wants to be treated as the opposite sex and schools will have to involve parents when it comes to decisions about their children.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly engages privacy rights of gender questioning students (mandatory parental disclosure), equal treatment and protection of an LGBT+ minority group in schools, and the balance between child autonomy and parental rights — all core O9 territory.

The policy mandates how schools must handle gender questioning pupils; this shapes the school environment for a specific group and plausibly affects their attendance, sense of safety, and educational attainment — a real verdict on educational opportunity.

Mandatory parental notification about a student's gender identity removes the student's control over disclosure of that information; this directly bears on privacy and bodily self-determination (O10 indicators), and the mechanism is concrete: the state compels schools to override the student's own disclosure choices.

membership_note: Two genuine bearings: O9 for the minority-protection and equal-treatment dimension, O10 for the privacy/bodily-autonomy dimension. These often conflict (as here), requiring separate verdicts. O7 is not in scope — the policy is about safeguarding/disclosure governance within schools, not attainment, standards, or skills.
